races.name: Attheraces.com/marketmovers Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Penfolds Grange
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse with two placed efforts at 8f on standard Lingfield; dropping back to 7f is a minor concern given half his recent history is at that longer trip, but Alfie Redman's 7lb claim keeps the weight competitive and he is in decent heart off a 19-day break.
runners_data.comment: Penfolds Grange shaped with plenty of promise when third two starts back and second on two occasions further back in his recent form, and he has run over today's trip; the concern is that ninth last time out suggests he may need to bounce back sharply.

runners_data.name: Optimatum
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's charge is a genuine hold-up type squeezed into midfield on the map by a crowded rear — 82 days off the track is notable and he has only one placed run from six on standard going, limiting confidence in a big first-time-back showing.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 82 days off, Optimatum does have distance experience to call on and rates slightly above his official mark, but two ninth-place finishes in recent outings are hard to ignore, making him a tough sell at this level.

runners_data.name: Daisy Roots
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who should secure a natural berth just off Rogue Dynasty's heels; Donagh Murphy's 5lb claim helps at the weights and she has been placed four times at 7f on standard Lingfield, making this trip and surface the ideal conditions for her to be competitive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Daisy Roots has shown enough consistency — three fourths and a second — to suggest she's competitive at this level, but converting that into a win remains the challenge; experience over today's trip and a 36-day break leave her fit and primed.

runners_data.name: Dancing Terror
runners_data.note: Comes into this as a horse who won over this course and distance on soft, has placed twice at 7f on standard, but has not run for 98 days — his true closer's style is masked by the redistribution, and trainer Stephanie Cassidy's 0/3 T14 record adds further caution to an already long layoff.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with his most recent effort a sixth and a second four starts back his only hint of form, Dancing Terror returns after a 98-day absence carrying 133 lb from stall 10 — it's hard to build a case here.

runners_data.name: Majestic Wave
runners_data.note: Has a single placed run from ten attempts at 7f on standard but has been placed only once on this surface overall; Simon Dow sends him out 22 days fresh and while the horse will want to race off the pace he may find his natural position harder to achieve in an eleven-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Majestic Wave has run over today's trip and bounced back with a runner-up finish last time out after a lean patch, and his rating of 72 marks him as a genuine threat here; the worry is he remains winless in recent starts and must prove that second was no fluke.

runners_data.name: Dandy Khan
runners_data.note: Strong course specialist with 13 of 15 career runs on standard going and four wins from those; Ashley Lewis takes the ride and Jim Boyle's stable is 2/10 over 14 days, giving this Jim Boyle-trained gelding some live angle — though he is a genuine hold-up runner racing in a shape that does not naturally favour him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a string of fifth and sixth-place finishes, Dandy Khan is hard to fancy on recent evidence, though she has run over today's trip before and returns on a sharp 13-day turnaround from stall one carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Sub Thirteen
runners_data.note: Olivia Tubb's 3lb claim helps a horse rated just 55; form includes a placed effort at 8f on standard and a recent second at the same trip, but dropping to 7f against better-rated rivals and racing as a true hold-up type in a slow-run race makes winning conditions difficult — the hood is noted.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Sub Thirteen does at least bring solid placed form to the table — second last time out and third two starts back — and he has experience over today's trip and conditions. Carrying 123 lb from stall six, a step back up in class looks the challenge.

runners_data.name: Ashford Hill
runners_data.note: Won at 7f on standard Lingfield on her last visit to this track and is 1W3P over the trip on this surface; Isobelle Chalmers' 7lb claim is a big help at 119lbs, and she holds genuine each-way claims if the pace holds — but she is a hold-up horse in a race that is likely to be controlled from the front.
runners_data.comment: Ashford Hill has struggled in her last three starts, finishing eighth and sixth before a third most recently, and 64 days off the track adds a fitness query. Has run over today's trip, and that sole win in her last five starts offers slim hope.

runners_data.name: Sahana
runners_data.note: The highest-rated runner at OR 70 and has been placed at 7f on standard Lingfield; David Simcock's 0/10 T14 record is a concern, but she has a win over this trip and surface and her hold-up style is at least consistent — she needs others to go fast enough for her to peel off the pace turning in.
runners_data.comment: Sahana showed she retains ability with a second two starts back, but fifth last time out and 39 days off temper expectations; she has run over today's trip and our rating has her mid-division of the field, so a midfield finish looks the likeliest outcome.

runners_data.name: Mister Mojito
runners_data.note: Carries a tongue-tie and has two wins at 7f on good or standard going; T J Kent's stable is a red-hot 3/3 over 14 days and Jack Callan's record warrants respect — a genuine hold-up runner who needs the pace to be honest, and the small but live trainer angle makes him interesting if the race develops favourably.
runners_data.comment: Mister Mojito has been knocking consistently on the door, finishing second last time out after some more modest efforts, and he returns in good order just 18 days later with distance experience to call on; the risk is he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Rogue Dynasty
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in this field and is 0W2P on standard going, but his consistent placed form (2-3-2-4-4) shows he rarely folds early; Mason Paetel navigates from the saddle and James Owen's 14/56 T14 strike rate is strong — he should get an uncontested lead and his ability to control tempo is the defining race-shape factor.
runners_data.comment: Rogue Dynasty has been knocking on the door in recent starts, finishing second last time out and a second three starts back, and she returns on a quick 12-day turnaround with experience over today's trip. Yet to win in her last five starts, but her consistency makes her the one to beat off a mark of 68.

races.paceDynamic: Rogue Dynasty is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with Daisy Roots the only other prominent-style runner, faces minimal pressure to her inside or outside across the first furlong, meaning she can dictate a controlled, honest gallop rather than a lung-busting fractions race. Daisy Roots will sit just off the pace and apply some pressure but not enough to turn this into a true test of stamina at 7f on standard Lingfield AW. The bulk of the field — Optimatum, Dancing Terror, Majestic Wave, Dandy Khan, Sub Thirteen and Ashford Hill — are all genuine hold-up types who have been pushed forward on the pace map because the rear is over-subscribed; in reality these horses will be ridden to get cover in mid-to-rear division and will need a sustained gallop to get competitive. With a single pace-setter controlling modest fractions, this shape most strongly favours horses who race prominently or just off the pace and can sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — front-to-prominent runners hold the structural edge here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rogue Dynasty Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Rogue Dynasty is allowed to stride clear from the gates and sets a measured, uncontested gallop.
scenarios.body: Rogue Dynasty dictates tempo from the front, Daisy Roots tracks in second, and the hold-up brigade are left with too much ground to make up against a horse who has never been headed at a crucial point; the moderate fractions suit a prominent, well-drawn runner who can quicken into the straight. Daisy Roots, racing naturally on the pace, is ideally placed to capitalise if Rogue Dynasty fades.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surge Too Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely true and the hold-up horses find clear daylight turning for home.
scenarios.body: A proper pace allows the back-markers to close, but most redistributed hold-up types in this field are not true closers and will need an unusually strong gallop that Rogue Dynasty is unlikely to set; the horses with genuine late-race form — Sahana and Mister Mojito — are the most plausible beneficiaries. Even so, the structural mismatch between natural style and mapped position reduces the probability of this shape delivering a winner from the rear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Battle Out
scenarios.trigger: If Daisy Roots challenges Rogue Dynasty vigorously from halfway, turning it into a sustained duel.
scenarios.body: A two-horse pace battle burns off the front-runners and leaves the door ajar for a prominent-to-midfield horse to swoop late; Sahana, with the highest OR at 70 and a course-and-distance placed run on her record, is best equipped to pick up the pieces. Penfolds Grange, placed twice at this track and trip on standard, could also fill a frame position if the leaders tire.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Wide Draw Trouble
scenarios.trigger: If the wider-drawn runners lose significant ground at the start and traffic problems scramble the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: With eleven runners over 7f at Lingfield, horses drawn wide who need a prominent position may find themselves shuffled back in the first two furlongs, and the resulting concertina effect leaves the race genuinely open. Dandy Khan's course experience (13 from 15 runs on standard going) gives him the adaptability to handle a messy race, though his OR of 60 remains a handicapping concern against higher-rated rivals.

watchPoints.text: Rogue Dynasty's ability to secure a clean, uncontested lead is the single most important factor — if she is allowed to stride clear at her own pace, the entire field faces a stern structural disadvantage and the race shape becomes very one-dimensional.

Dandy Khan's trainer form (Jim Boyle 2/10 T14) combined with his strong course record on standard going makes him a horse to keep an eye on in the market — if he shortens late, it may reflect stable confidence that outweighs his hold-up style disadvantage.

Mister Mojito's stable is 3/3 in the last 14 days for TJ Kent — a small but perfect record — and the tongue-tie angle means any unexpected improvement here could catch punters off guard if pace develops to suit hold-up horses.

The redistribution of six true hold-up horses into midfield on the pace map means the final two furlongs could become congested if all of them make their move simultaneously — watch for horses such as Sahana and Penfolds Grange who have the clearest profile to pick through traffic late.

Sub Thirteen and Ashford Hill, both on low weights with claiming apprentices, could be underestimated outsiders if the race deteriorates into a tactical crawl and the field bunches — their claims and course form at 7f on standard give them marginal each-way relevance at price.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 EBF Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race) (Div 1) (AWT)
Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Ebf Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (Ebf Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race) (Div II)
John Cunliffe Obf 80th Birthday Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Twilight Madness
runners_data.note: True hold-up type who has placed twice at 6f on this Standard surface; Charlie Tucker's 7lb claim is useful off OR-63, and 18 days since last run is a workable freshen-up, though he must navigate a congested closing pack.
runners_data.comment: Twilight Madness landed a win four starts back and posted a third and second earlier in the sequence, showing he's capable at this level; drawn in stall two and carrying 133 lb, the worry is his last two runs have both been well below that form.

runners_data.name: Just Jump
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll has landed 3 from 35 in the last 14 days showing stable form; this horse won over 5f at Good recently but at 6f on Standard the style-fit concern is real — a genuine closer pushed onto the map at midfield, he cannot guarantee his preferred rear berth in this field.
runners_data.comment: Just Jump arrives here on the back of a win two starts back and has run over today's trip, with 33 days between runs leaving him fresh; the concern is that refusal three starts back raises a jumping question mark he'll need to answer.

runners_data.name: Havana Sky
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop sends a horse with 14 from 15 similar-going runs, solid course familiarity, and a hood; yet he is a natural hold-up operator who will find others between him and the back markers, making his race entirely dependent on late gaps appearing.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Havana Sky heads here 22 days after a seventh, and while he has run over today's trip and our rating edges his official mark, he ranks eighth of eleven — modest recent form makes a significant step forward hard to foresee.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Moon
runners_data.note: Denis Coakley's runner has five recent place efforts including wins at 6f on Good, but his last two runs on similar ground produced 8th-place finishes and he arrives having raced just 12 days ago; his natural style belongs at the back yet this field forces him forward where he has not flourished.
runners_data.comment: Phoenix Moon has finished eighth in each of her last two starts, making her tough to fancy despite a third and a win in earlier recent outings; she has run over today's trip before, and 12 days between runs suggests she is at least fit and ready.

runners_data.name: Balon d'Or
runners_data.note: Simon Dow's five-year-old has no wins and no places from six similar-going runs — the stat that stands out most; forced into a midfield position that does not suit his trailing instincts, and carries a pace headgear flag without convincing recent evidence to support confidence here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Balon d'Or does at least have experience over today's trip and arrives here 26 days fresh, but a fourth two starts back is the sole bright spot in otherwise modest form, and 130 lb from stall nine makes life no easier.

runners_data.name: Elvetham
runners_data.note: The sole genuine front-runner in the field; Conrad Allen has him reappearing quickly (5 days) which can indicate freshness or need, and the blinkers flag is noted, but his ability to lead without pressure is the key race-shaping factor — OR-58 gives him a competitive weight.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Elvetham faces a stiff ask here; third two starts back offers a crumb of comfort, and he has run over today's trip, but five days between runs is a brisk turnaround for a horse yet to find the winner's enclosure in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Master Dandy
runners_data.note: Two wins and five places from 14 similar-going runs tells a positive course/going story, and tongue-tie plus blinkers suggest he needs assistance to focus; genuinely a hold-up horse who is mapped forward under redistribution pressure, he works best when given time and room late.

runners_data.name: Vitalline
runners_data.note: Josephine Gordon rides a horse with three wins from 15 similar-going runs — the highest strike rate in the field on this surface profile; tongue-tie and blinkers are engaged, and at OR-52 the weight advantage is real, but this is a natural closer who needs the field to open up rather than bunch.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Vitalline's recent form is patchy — ninth last time out and largely struggling in his last six, bar a win two starts back. Has run over today's trip and returns after 30 days, but it's hard to make a case from here.

runners_data.name: Reposado
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's four-year-old has two placed efforts at 6f on Good but limited Lingfield AW exposure; arrives 32 days fresh and has shown a tendency to race hold-up, not replicated on the map — a genuine closer who must find clear air in the final stages.
runners_data.comment: Reposado has experience over today's trip and returns after 32 days, shaped by two consecutive seconds four and five starts back — though winless in his last six, our rating of 76 marks him out as the one to beat from stall 4 off 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Express Train
runners_data.note: Richard Phillips sends a horse whose last five runs include a third at 6f/Standard — his only creditable effort recently; a genuine back-of-field type pushed onto the midfield map, and with a poor overall strike rate on similar going (0 wins from 6 recent runs), confidence is limited.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Express Train does at least bring distance experience to the table and is fresh enough after 33 days, but his recent slide — unplaced last time out after a third three starts back — makes him hard to fancy from stall 12 off 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Style King
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani partners a horse who won last time at 6f/Standard and placed at 5f/Standard — two ticks of form relevance; although mapped as a hold-up type, the recent win shows tactical flexibility, and he could exploit a prominent position if traffic allows.
runners_data.comment: A winner last time out and he has run over today's trip, but that eighth and sixth in recent starts expose some inconsistency; 29 days off and 133 lb from stall 10 make this a guarded each-way read at best.

runners_data.name: Federal Envoy
runners_data.note: Charlie Clover has fired 2 from 8 runners in the last 14 days and this horse placed at 6f on Good; however, last four runs since that placed effort have been disappointing, and at OR-63 top weight he must outrun a modest recent profile to justify optimism.
runners_data.comment: Federal Envoy arrives on the back of a second two starts back, and our rating of 68 nudges him ahead of his official mark, suggesting he's capable of better — yet he's winless in his last six starts, and that lack of a win is the nagging concern.

races.paceDynamic: Elvetham is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 12-runner field and should lead comfortably from stall, setting a controlled, honest gallop over Lingfield's straight 6f without any genuine pace pressure to force him wide or burn early. With no rival able to match his position from the gate, the fractions will be measured rather than frantic — Elvetham shapes as a genuine factor throughout rather than a pacemaker who will be swallowed up. The field behind him is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types: Just Jump, Havana Sky, Phoenix Moon, Balon d'Or, Master Dandy, Vitalline and Express Train are all true closers pushed forward on the map simply because the rear is overcrowded, meaning they cannot all get their natural position and several must race further forward than ideal. This race shape — a lone leader at controlled fractions, a congested closing pack lacking room to express themselves — favours horses who can race prominently or make a forward move from midfield early enough to avoid the late traffic, and penalises true hold-up types who need gaps that a bunched field rarely gives.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Elvetham Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Elvetham leads cleanly and no rival applies early pressure, allowing him to dictate a sustainable pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Elvetham bowls along on a fair clip with no challenger to his inside or outside, conserving energy into the straight before finding extra when the field closes; his OR-58 mark looks lenient if he gets an uncontested lead on this flat, gallop-friendly surface.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Pair Clear Late
scenarios.trigger: If Elvetham is joined by one of the redistributed midfielders who breaks forward aggressively, creating a genuine pace duel that still suits those tracking closely.
scenarios.body: The pace quickens and Elvetham battles gamely but a horse tracking in second or third slot picks up the rhythm to challenge; horses with tactical versatility who can sit just off the pace without burning early reserves come into their own.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Elvetham's gallop is genuinely strong enough to open the track up and the hold-up horses find clear daylight in the closing furlong.
scenarios.body: The field strings out and a true closer with pace reserves gets a gap on the inside or outside rail in the final 150 yards; this scenario requires the field to thin and the pace to have been brisk enough to stop the leaders — neither is guaranteed given one front-runner and multiple displaced hold-ups.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple displaced hold-up horses push forward competing for prominent positions early, creating a scrambled pace that collapses in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The redistribution effect fires: several natural closers forced wide and forward burn energy they cannot afford, the pace spikes and then drops, and the race degenerates into a tactical mess where tactical intelligence from jockey and horse matters most.

watchPoints.text: Elvetham has run just 5 days ago — watch the market closely; if he drifts significantly it may indicate the quick turnaround is a concern, which would remove the only front-runner and fundamentally alter the race shape.

Multiple hold-up horses (Just Jump, Havana Sky, Master Dandy, Phoenix Moon) are displaced onto the midfield map — watch the early stages for a squeeze or crowding on the inside rail as these horses are forced wider than ideal, increasing collision risk in the first two furlongs.

Vitalline's 15-from-15 similar-going profile is statistically striking but she is at OR-52 in a competitive handicap — watch whether Josephine Gordon elects to drop her out regardless of the map, which would leave her with a significant amount of ground to make up in a compressed final furlong.

Style King won last time out at 6f/Standard with Marco Ghiani aboard — watch whether he travels smoothly in the first half of the race, as a horse with recent form on this exact surface and trip is one of the few runners whose profile genuinely fits the likely race shape without redistribution caveats.

Federal Envoy and Reposado both carry the hg:p flag (prominent tendency noted in headgear records) despite being mapped as hold-up types — watch the early break to see if either pushes forward unexpectedly, which could create a two-horse pace scenario and alter the fractions significantly.
